query: For as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys intended for magnetic refrigeration, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their magnetocaloric response and hysteresis during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles? Earlier work focused mainly on arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons, where an ordered single-phase hexagonal state undergoes a first-order magnetostructural transition that produces a large but sharp and hysteretic entropy change; these bulk forms also have limited heat-exchange rates because of their low surface-to-volume ratio. Prior searches have largely emphasized composition-dependent changes in transition temperature or response amplitude, with most studies pursuing only one optimization variable. Under the constraints of avoiding rare-earth elements, retaining mechanical stability and low cost, enabling rapid heat exchange, and limiting hysteretic losses, specify one controlled intervention that would distinguish the proposed governing explanation from alternatives, the predicted observations relative to the as-deposited baseline, the boundaries over which those predictions should hold, the prior observations that support the hypothesis, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In as-deposited nanocrystalline Fe–Mn–Ni–Ge–Si thin-film high-entropy alloys, the magnitude of the magnetocaloric entropy change and its field-cycle hysteresis are governed primarily by the degree of chemical short-range ordering between Ge/Si and transition-metal species on the 2c site of the hexagonal Ni2In-type lattice; increasing that local order strengthens magneto-elastic coupling, which simultaneously (i) raises the latent heat of the magnetostructural transition, enlarging |ΔSm|, and (ii) increases the energy barrier for the first-order transformation, enlarging hysteresis losses.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, non-equiatomic Fe43Mn32Ni15Ge6Si4 (at. %) nanocrystalline films (≤5 µm thick) sputtered onto Cu foils; single-phase hexagonal Ni2In-type structure with limited chemical short-range order and high microstrain.
generation.intervention: Post-deposition isothermal anneal at 573 K for 2 h under Ar to promote short-range ordering while avoiding grain coarsening or secondary-phase precipitation.
generation.conditions: Magnetocaloric measurements in 0–1 T cyclic magnetic fields, 250–350 K temperature range; film adhered to Cu substrate to ensure identical heat-exchange conditions before and after anneal.
generation.structural_mediator: Increase in 100/101 superlattice reflection intensity and reduction of Warren-type peak broadening in synchrotron X-ray diffraction, indicating enhanced Ge/Si–TM ordering and reduced microstrain.
generation.mechanism: Enhanced site ordering increases exchange-striction and changes the elastic modulus mismatch across the martensitic interface, raising the magneto-elastic coupling coefficient. The higher coupling delivers a larger latent heat (thus larger ΔSm) but simultaneously increases the nucleation barrier, widening the thermal/magnetic hysteresis loop.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-deposited baseline, the annealed films will show: 1) 30–50 % higher peak |ΔSm| at ≈300 K under 1 T (e.g., from ~3 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ to 4–5 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹), 2) an approximately two-fold increase in magnetic hysteresis loss area (e.g., from ~0.1 to ≥0.2 J kg⁻¹ per cycle), and 3) a measurable growth (≥50 %) in the 100 superlattice peak intensity with only modest grain-size change (<20 %).
generation.baseline: As-deposited films: peak |ΔSm| ≈3 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 1 T, hysteresis loss ≈0.1 J kg⁻¹ per cycle, weak or absent 100 superlattice reflection in XRD.
generation.boundary: Prediction expected to hold for Fe–Mn–Ni–(Ge,Si) compositions whose martensitic transition lies between 250–350 K and for anneals below 0.6 T_melt (<700 K) that do not induce secondary phases or recrystallization beyond 100 nm grains. Outside this window (e.g., higher anneal temperatures or very different Ge/Si ratios), competing phase separation may dominate and break the correlation.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of the |ΔSm| enhancement and hysteresis broadening is estimated; limited prior data on thin-film HEA ordering kinetics means quantitative values could vary by ±50 %.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three identical sputtered Fe43Mn32Ni15Ge6Si4 films. Sample A: keep as-deposited. Sample B: anneal 573 K/2 h (targeted ordering). Sample C: anneal 573 K/2 h then rapid water quench to freeze in any developed order. Characterize structure (synchrotron XRD Rietveld refinement for superlattice peaks; TEM selected-area diffraction for ordering), then measure ΔSm(T, H) and hysteresis from isothermal magnetization loops in 0–1 T field cycles.
measurements: Superlattice (100) peak intensity ratio to fundamental (101)
Microstrain and grain size from Williamson–Hall analysis
Magnetic-field hysteresis loss (area between increasing and decreasing M–T curves)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If samples with significantly higher short-range order (≥50 % increase in 100 peak intensity) do NOT show a concomitant increase (≥15 %) in both |ΔSm| and hysteresis loss, OR if |ΔSm| and hysteresis increase without any detectable rise in ordering, then the hypothesis is falsified.
